chapter: New York, the Lafayette and the Cotton Club
title: Competition among bands and Cab Calloway at the rehearsal
summary: Crawford says rival bands did not want them, and Cab Calloway, also managed by Mills, came to Cotton Club rehearsals.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: All of those kind of things. And now like, you say when you got to -- when you all were in New York there was a great deal of competititon between the bands, wasn't there?
Oh, yeah, they didn't want us -- they didn't want us in this (inaudible).

Because you might take jobs that they would be getting? And when you all started working for Irving Mills, you say you all started working with Irving Mills when Duke Ellington and Cab Calloway were with him too.

Yeah, Cab Calloway and Duke worked for Mills. And, of course, Cab came to a couple of our rehearsals when we were breaking in -- in the Cotton Club, practicing, rehearsing the show and whatnot, looking sharp. No wonder old Moms Mabley said (inaudible) -- Moms Mahley, it was in her act, her man was Cab Calloway. Of course, he let his hair float down over his face. Oh, Cab was a sharp guy, one thing I can say about him. And that's why I'm sorry I missed that Beaux Arts ball. He's usually there.

And I was going -- I went out and bought me a brand new modern tuxedo, patent leather pumps, shirts, all that stuff. Yeah, I did that. And I just -- well, it's just over, the 10th. Oh, well, I must have changed my mind.
